carbon_policy_signal.item: EU green-transition chief proposes new oil tax and joint debt mechanism for climate resilience funding; signals regulatory capex intensification.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: New carbon/energy tax mechanisms raise fossil-generator operating costs and increase regulatory capex burden, structurally supporting EUA bid and raising marginal generation cost.

freshness_caveat: Coal data is 251 days stale (as of 2025-12-26); clean dark is 246 days stale (as of 2025-12-31). Fuel-switch economics and clean-dark spread trend may not reflect current regime. Rely on TTF, GB/DE power, and clean spark (fresh) for position signals.
risk_flags: GB Power at 96th-percentile (163.66 EUR/MWh) with 23.1% daily jump; nuclear outage risk from rising water-scarcity temperatures could extend premium into Cal+1.
Hormuz closure scenario would disrupt ~20% of seaborne LNG flows; TTF already at 75th-percentile (73.63 EUR/MWh) — tail-risk premium building on military escalation.
Coal at 7th-percentile (96.0 USD/t, 251 days stale) and clean dark at 47th (27.95 EUR/MWh, 246 days stale); fuel-switch dynamics obscured by data lag.
US LNG capacity surge to 17.4 Bcf/d offsets Hormuz premium via NW Europe arb, creating bidirectional gas/power volatility.

base.summary: GB power holds premium on nuclear climate stress; TTF stable as US LNG arb pressures offset Hormuz tail-risk.

downside.summary: Hormuz diplomatic resolution; US LNG export ramp sustains NW Europe arb supply; mild weather reduces nuclear cooling stress.

upside.summary: Hormuz military escalation triggers LNG supply shock; EU nuclear outage cluster reduces baseload; data-center demand spikes.

themes: Nuclear thermal stress and data-center load pressure EU baseload
Hormuz geopolitical tail-risk vs. US LNG supply glut
GB power premium persisting despite coal floor at 7th-percentile
Policy intensification signals on carbon tax and green capex
top_drivers: GB Power at 96th-percentile driven by nuclear thermal-stress outages and data-center baseload surge colliding with summer cooling constraints.
Hormuz escalation tail-risk premia on TTF front (75th-pctile) offset by US LNG export glut (17.4 Bcf/d); bidirectional volatility in NW Europe gas/power.

Clean Spark at 93rd-percentile (41.04 EUR/MWh) reflects coal floor (7th-pctile, 96.0 USD/t) and gas premium (75th-pctile TTF) in fuel-switch regime; data lag on coal (251 days old) obscures trend confirmation.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 96th-percentile amid nuclear climate stress and data-center demand surge; Hormuz escalation threatens LNG supply and TTF, offsetting US LNG export growth.

watchlist.why: US–Iran strikes could trigger LNG flow disruption and 20%+ TTF spike; risk premium already embedded in current 75th-pctile level.
Rising water-scarcity outages reduce baseload, extending GB/DE power premiums; multi-year structural demand from data centers amplifies tightness.

watchlist.metric: US LNG export ramp (17.4 Bcf/d H1 2026)
watchlist.why: 23% surge eases NW Europe LNG arb; downward TTF pressure via substitution effect, but Hormuz risk creates price-floor asymmetry.

watchlist.metric: Von der Leyen SOTEU speech & EU budget carbon-tax proposal
watchlist.why: New green capex financing and carbon-pricing mechanisms could restructure power/gas curve expectations; signals EUA structural bid into 2027.
